verdict.rationale: Zulip documents its own programmatic, UI-free interfaces: an API with endpoints such as sending messages, and an interactive bot framework that can be deployed to stay up on a server via the Zulip Botserver. Together these support headless automation, but nothing in the evidence shows CI-specific usage. missing for 10: documented CI/pipeline integration or a headless CLI, examples of running automation in CI, independent or hands-on corroboration of headless automation workflows.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Zulip’s API has a powerful framework for interactive bots that react to messages in Zulip. You can write and run a custom bot, or run an existing Zulip bot.
Eventually, you’ll probably want to run it in a production environment where it’ll stay up, by deploying it on a server using the Zulip Botserver.
